Manual trial operation

Charge the closing spring
Insert the manual closing 36 spring charging handle (71) to its inlet (7) and 
move it up and down about 8 times up to charged-discharged indicator (6) 
indicating charged

Close the breaker
Pull the closing button (17), the breaker is closed, and open-closed indicator 
(8) indicates "closed" and charged-discharged indicator (6) changes to 
"discharged"

Open the breaker
Pull the trip button (16), the breaker is open, and open-closed indicator (8) 
changes to "open". Repeat these operation for several times and confirm the 
breaker to be operated normally.

Electrical trial operation

Connect the control 
circuit
Connect the test terminal (72) or secondary plug to the breaker, then the motor 
(43) starts to charge the closing spring (36), when the closing spring (36) has 
been charged, charged-discharged indicator (6) indicates "charged"

Close the breaker
Operate the control switch for closing, the breaker is closed, open-closed 
indicator (8) indicates "closed" and charged-discharged indicator (6) changes to 
"discharged" and then the motor (43) starts to charge the closing spring (36) 
immediately. Therefore the closing spring (36) is recharged, and 
charged-discharged indicator (6) indicates "charged"

Open the Breaker
Operate the control switch for open, the breaker is open, open-closed indicator 
(8) changes to "open". If you operate the control switch for closing immediately 
after operation for open, the breaker may be closed because of the closing 
spring (36) having been charged
Repeat above operation 2 and 3 for several times and confirm the breaker to be 
operated normally.

sections.text:
Properties of sF6 
gas
SF6 gas weights approximately 5.5 times as much as air.

Being colorless, 
odorless, and inert in its in its ordinary 
conditions, this gas is highly stabilized. This gas is liquefied at -62C 
under atmospheric pressure and at 0C under pressure of 12 kg/cm2 respectively. 
Since fptm type gcb uses gas at a pressure of 4 kg/cm2, liquefaction 
temperature of the gas is as low as about -37C, requiring no heater. Further, 
since the coefficient of heat transfer of SF6 gas exceeds that of air under the 
same condition approximately by a factor of 2.5 any temperature rise in case of 
energizing is low compared with the case of using air. Also, although it varies 
depending upon the shape of electrode, the dielectric strength of SF6 gas in a 
uniform electric field is 2.5 to 3 times as great as great as that of the 
atmosphere, becoming equal to that of insulating oil at an approximate pressure 
of 2 kg/cm2 (at 20C). Being considerably great in electron bending capability, 
sf6 gas displays splendid arc-extinguishing performance

Precaution of 
sF6 
gas 
handling 
and 
safety

Regarding the poisonous characteristic of sf6, the 
result of various experiments conducted on which rabbits and mice revealed that 
sf6 gas itself is inert and produces no poisonous effect on the human body. 
Concerning tests on its poisonous character, it is stipulated that mice shall be 
able to withstand without hindrance the atmosphere of gaseous mixture consisting 
of 75% sf6 and 25% oxygen for a period of 14 to 16 hours

Decomposition products produced by arc discharge 
(HF,SF4,SF2,S2F2, etc) are harmful. Therefore, necessary steps have been taken 
by Hitachi to minimize these products, such as controlling of moisture in the 
interrupter to 150 ppm by volume or less (moisture in the atmosphere is 
approximately 20.000ppm by volume) and the absorption of decomposition products 
by absorbent (synthetic zeolite). Although a small amount of powdery sulfide and 
fluoride is found in the container inside the tank after breaking a large 
current, the above power has produced to harmful affect on the human body so 
far. It is advisable, however, always to wear a mask and gloves for a detailed 
inspection or contact replacement

SF6 
gas 
is approximately 5.5 
times 
as 
heavy 
as 
air

It is a colorless, odorless, inert gas. Consequently, care should 
be exercised with ventilation when handling this gas, as fer as possible avoid 
handling the gas in an enclosed room or pit. Should a large amount of sf6 gas 
escape, it floats on the lower layer, so that there is a possibility that only a 
large amount of SF6 gas is released in a narrow or improperly ventilated space 
during an inspection, there is possibility of oxygen shortage. Exercise the 
utmost care

Properties of sF6 
gas
SF6 gas weights approximately 5.5 times as much as air.
Being colorless, 
odorless, and inert in its in its ordinary 
conditions, this gas is highly stabilized. This gas is liquefied at -62C 
under atmospheric pressure and at 0C under pressure of 12 kg/cm2 respectively. 
Since fptm type gcb uses gas at a pressure of 4 kg/cm2, liquefaction 
temperature of the gas is as low as about -37C, requiring no heater. Further, 
since the coefficient of heat transfer of SF6 gas exceeds that of air under the 
same condition approximately by a factor of 2.5 any temperature rise in case of 
energizing is low compared with the case of using air. Also, although it varies 
depending upon the shape of electrode, the dielectric strength of SF6 gas in a 
uniform electric field is 2.5 to 3 times as great as great as that of the 
atmosphere, becoming equal to that of insulating oil at an approximate pressure 
of 2 kg/cm2 (at 20C). Being considerably great in electron bending capability, 
sf6 gas displays splendid arc-extinguishing performance
Precaution of 
sF6 
gas 
handling 
and 
safety
Regarding the poisonous characteristic of sf6, the 
result of various experiments conducted on which rabbits and mice revealed that 
sf6 gas itself is inert and produces no poisonous effect on the human body. 
Concerning tests on its poisonous character, it is stipulated that mice shall be 
able to withstand without hindrance the atmosphere of gaseous mixture consisting 
of 75% sf6 and 25% oxygen for a period of 14 to 16 hours
Decomposition products produced by arc discharge 
(HF,SF4,SF2,S2F2, etc) are harmful. Therefore, necessary steps have been taken 
by Hitachi to minimize these products, such as controlling of moisture in the 
interrupter to 150 ppm by volume or less (moisture in the atmosphere is 
approximately 20.000ppm by volume) and the absorption of decomposition products 
by absorbent (synthetic zeolite). Although a small amount of powdery sulfide and 
fluoride is found in the container inside the tank after breaking a large 
current, the above power has produced to harmful affect on the human body so 
far. It is advisable, however, always to wear a mask and gloves for a detailed 
inspection or contact replacement
